sources.name: tiny
sources.covers: the simplest possible export: three rows, one month, one sheet

sources.name: empty
sources.covers: zero rows: is_empty on the shape, and what a plan does with nothing to place

sources.name: single_row
sources.covers: one row: a header plus a single data row, the smallest non-empty sheet

sources.name: multi_year
sources.covers: about five years at three-day spacing: one sheet per year, and period ordering

sources.name: undated
sources.covers: a third of the rows undated: the UNDATED bucket, which must come last under BOTH period orders

sources.name: all_undated
sources.covers: every row undated: an export with no dated bucket at all

sources.name: int_yymm
sources.covers: the two-digit-year window at its boundaries, and leading zeros that are not truncation

sources.name: int_yyyymmdd
sources.covers: a leap day, and the two days a year boundary is made of

sources.name: zoned
sources.covers: a named zone moving a row into the previous YEAR: rows 1 and 2 are the same UTC day and belong in different workbooks

sources.name: wall_clock
sources.covers: naive timestamps read as a wall clock, with no zone consulted

sources.name: overflow
sources.covers: one period with more rows than the tight profile allows per worksheet: overflow fragments and part_index

sources.name: dtypes
sources.covers: every scalar dtype at its boundary values: what the ToExcel conversion does to each, which is the thing worth eyeballing

sources.name: odd_names
sources.covers: column names Polars would read as a wildcard and a regex, plus a non-ASCII header; all legal in Parquet
